title: Recorded symptoms classify persistent smell and taste complaints after COVID-19
summary: In a 413-person retrospective questionnaire dataset, learned models classified reported smell and taste complaints persisting beyond four weeks. The selected 83-record test reported AUCs up to 0.96 for taste and 0.97 for smell. This does not establish an early prospective forecast or improved treatment.

source_review.scope: Original primary clinical design, model training, persistence Results and Table8; archived publication metadata

evidence.tested: The study used a random 330-record training/validation set and 83-record test. Persistence predictors included symptom continuation after two weeks and smell/taste loss during infection.
evidence.unknown: The study is described as cross-sectional and does not establish that every predictor was recorded before outcome ascertainment. Whole-data feature ranking and test-informed algorithm selection limit generalization. Confusion-matrix paragraph denominators and percentages conflict with Table8; this record uses only table/ROC AUC ranges, not its accuracy or sensitivity claims. No external clinical validation, calibrated population risk or causal effect is established.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted tree ensembles map questionnaire and symptom features to recorded persistent-complaint labels; the represented result is retrospective clinical-label evaluation.
